newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Russian border guards kill two on Afghan border.
newsitem.headline: Russian border guards kill two on Afghan border.

text.p: Russian border guards killed two people trying to cross into Tajikistan from nearby Afghanistan late on Thursday, a Russian military official said on Friday.
"Two armed persons were liquidated by fire from a Russian border guards helicopter," the officer told Reuters in the Tajik capital Dushanbe.
The two were killed as they tried to cross the border Pyandzh River, around 200 km (125 miles) south of Dushanbe, he said.
Some 20,000 Russian troops are stationed in Tajikistan, viewing themselves as a shield against the possible advent of militant, Taleban-type Islam from neighbouring Afghanistan.
Last Friday, Tajikistan's secular government and the united Islamic opposition signed a final peace agreement in Moscow, putting an end to a bitter four-year civil war.
But the peace in the Central Asian state is often disturbed by maverick armed bands and drug traders operating out of their bases in Afghanistan.
